column3: NFIB Optimism Index will drop below 95 by June 2026 as tariff reality hits small business sentiment
column8: MISSED, and this is the most expensive miss in the POP set — 80% ex-ante on the wrong side. NFIB Small Business Optimism JUNE 2026 = 97.4, UP 2.1 points, and NFIB describes it as "nearing its 52-year average of 98.0," driven by improving expectations for business conditions and real sales. The prediction required a drop BELOW 95 by June 2026. The Apr-17 upgrade 65% -> 80% (taken off a March 95.8 reading) was upgrading INTO the reversal.
column9: RESOLVED 2026-07-24, parent-level. CALIBRATION LESSON worth carrying: an 80% call was placed on a sentiment index continuing a direction, one month after a single print approached the threshold. Sentiment indices mean-revert; this is the [[feedback_single_month_subcomponent_skepticism]] family applied to a survey rather than a data subcomponent. MATERIAL FOR THE PARENT: NFIB at 97.4 and rising is a genuine counter-signal to the CARL small-business stress leg (CRL-15/16/17), not just a POP-local miss.

column3: Restaurant sector will see 700+ QSR chain location closures (Wendy's + Pizza Hut + Papa John's combined) confirmed in H1 2026
column8: MISSED. Graded on the ACTUAL-CLOSURE basis. Confirmed H1-2026 closures = 390 vs a 700 bar: Wendy's 289 (H1 gross US, WEN Q2'26 earnings 8/14/26; cross-check US units 5,805 3/28/26 -> 5,724 6/30/26, Q2 opened 21 US so Q2 gross 102; YoY US -243 from 5,967) + Papa John's 101 (NA program-to-date thru Q2'26, PZZA Q2'26 call: 'we've closed 101 of the planned 300 North American restaurants') + Pizza Hut UNMEASURABLE. ROBUST: even crediting Pizza Hut its FULL announced 250, total = 640 < 700, so the miss does not depend on closing the Pizza Hut instrument gap. DEFECT 1 (basis undefined): 'closures ... confirmed in H1' never specified announced-vs-effected; on the ANNOUNCEMENT basis (300-350+250+200=750-800) it was already true on 2026-04-17 -- the same day confidence was raised to 95%, i.e. zero information content at upgrade. Either reading denies this a win. DEFECT 2 (leg has no published instrument): YUM does not disclose a Pizza Hut U.S. unit count. Q2'26 10-Q (yum-20260630.htm) shows Division 19,985 units 6/30/26 vs 19,768 6/30/25 = +1% GROWING; only US granularity is '70% of which are located outside the U.S.' (rounded). Same failure class as CRL-16's 8/10 MISS -- declared Instrument named a source TYPE ('company disclosures'), not a series. Failure pattern: ANNOUNCEMENT-VS-REALIZATION BASIS MISMATCH (bar set off announcement arithmetic, graded against realized counts). Related to CRL-01 'direction right, magnitude wrong' -- closures are real and large, the 700 level was not.
column9: NEAR-CONFIRMED at company level. Wendy's + Pizza Hut + Papa John's alone = 750-800. Adding Jack in Box, Noodles, Bahama Breeze = 944-1,049 FY total. Invalidation: companies reverse closure plans (very unlikely given company filings/earnings guidance).
column10: UNRESOLVABLE AS WRITTEN on one leg: Wendy's = WEN 10-Q/earnings US unit count (published); Papa John's = PZZA NA unit count + closure-program disclosure (published); Pizza Hut U.S. = NOT PUBLISHED by YUM at any cadence.

column3: SBA 7(a) default rate will breach 5% (ORANGE threshold) by Q4 2026 driven by 2020-21 vintage loan maturities plus tariff-stressed 2022-23 vintage
column7: Apr 17 update: Confidence REDUCED from 55% to 50%. IEEPA tariff removal + IEEPA refunds ($166B, many to small businesses) may provide enough liquidity to push some defaults past year-end. Section 122 10% still pressures margins but less than IEEPA 125%+ [FLAGGED WRONG pre-Apr-17 — actual ~20%; correct at Jul-24 refresh]. Path from 3.4% to 5% still requires 160bps; now less certain timing.
column9: ⚠️ COHERENCE BUG FOUND AND FIXED 2026-07-24: POP-P06 (SBA 7(a) default >5% by Q4-2026) sat at 50% while the CARL parent CRL-15 (SBA 7(a) default >6.5% by Q4-2026) sat at 65%. That is impossible — >5% is strictly implied by >6.5%, so P(>5%) MUST be >= P(>6.5%). A lower threshold cannot carry lower confidence than a higher one on the same series and date. FIX: POP-P06 50 -> 55 and CARL CRL-15 65 -> 35, which restores monotonicity and reflects that the series is at 3.7% with two quarters left. GENERAL LESSON: nested thresholds on the same series/date must be checked for monotonicity across the parent and sub-agent ledgers — nobody was looking at both at once.
